title: Content Safety
readOnlyNotice: Only company owners can change Content Safety settings. You can still review the current policy and recent activity.

hero.title: Content Safety
hero.summaryOff: Messages and files are not scanned
hero.offBody: Secrets, IDs, and personal details can slip into chat and files. Turn protection on to catch them before they leave.
hero.privacyNote: Your team sees a short note when something is flagged. Raw message text is never stored — only a fingerprint and a masked snippet.
hero.learnMore: How it works for your team

choices.carefulHint: Stricter catches more edge cases; looser means fewer interruptions.
choices.outcomeHint: Pick what happens for people on your team.

customize.title: Customize checks
customize.hint: Rules, recent activity, company bans, and the AI checker

sections.policyHint: Master switch and how carefully we scan
sections.statsHint: How often Content Safety stepped in
sections.statsEmpty: No hits yet — quiet is often a good sign.
sections.builtinRulesHint: Turn off checks your team does not need. Everything starts on.
sections.customPatternsHint: Block internal codenames, project names, or phrases unique to your company
sections.llmClassifierHint: Optional smart pass for content fixed rules might miss
sections.recentEventsHint: Latest Content Safety events in this company

sensitivity.label: How careful
sensitivity.labelHint: How eagerly the scanner flags borderline matches.
sensitivity.lenientDesc: Only clear, high-risk matches. Fewer interruptions.
sensitivity.balancedDesc: Recommended. Catches most secrets and personal data.
sensitivity.strictDesc: Flags borderline cases too. More prompts for your team.

mode.label: When something is found
mode.enforceDesc: Blocks risky sends. Low-risk matches only show a warning.
mode.redactDesc: Replace sensitive bits with placeholders (e.g. [EMAIL_1]) and send the rest.
mode.spanDef: Only the sensitive fragment is replaced — the rest of the message stays as written.

settings.notifyOwnersDesc: Owners can review a summary of Content Safety events. Individual message text is never included.

transparency.title: What your team sees
transparency.body1: People get a calm note: a quick toast for warnings, and a dialog that stops the send for blocks.
transparency.body2: We never store the raw message. Only a one-way fingerprint and a masked excerpt are recorded when a rule matches.
transparency.body3: Platform admins can review these recorded events with the team and member attached.

customPatterns.empty: No company bans yet. Add a project codename or internal phrase to catch it in chat and files.
customPatterns.name: Label (optional)

llm.title: AI checker
llm.intro: An optional smart pass that catches sensitive business content fixed rules might miss — deal terms, salary packages, internal codenames in free text.
llm.guidancePrompt: What should count as sensitive here?
llm.guidancePromptHint: Describe your company policy in plain language. Use Enhance to tighten it into clear flag/allow rules.
llm.guidancePromptPlaceholder: e.g. Flag named customer contracts with dollar figures; allow public product docs…

enhance.empty: Write a short draft first, then enhance

llm.thresholdsLabel: What to do when the AI flags content
llm.thresholdsHint: Pick the response for each risk level.
llm.thresholdConfidentialDef: Sensitive but lower risk — e.g. internal-only notes.
llm.thresholdRestrictedDef: Highest risk — e.g. credentials or regulated personal data.

test.title: Try a sample
test.placeholder: Paste a sample message to see what would be flagged…
test.needsEnabled: Turn on the AI checker to run a test.

violationModal.titleConfirm: One thing worth a second look
violationModal.titleRedact: We can tidy this before sending
violationModal.intro: We spotted something that looks like sensitive info you might not want to share. Take a quick look before sending.
violationModal.redactHint: Sensitive spans will be replaced with placeholders before sending.
violationModal.blockHint: This message won't be sent until you adjust the highlighted part. You can tidy it and try again.
violationModal.groupedHint_one: {{count}} similar place in this message or file — shown as one item.
violationModal.groupedHint_other: {{count}} similar places in this message or file — shown as one item.
violationModal.summaryLine: {{findings}} findings across {{types}} types — grouped below so you can scan quickly.

explainer.line1: We check messages for things like passwords, keys, or personal details that are easy to paste by accident.
explainer.line2: Your message text is never stored. We only keep a one-way fingerprint and a masked snippet when something matches.
explainer.line3: This check is set up by your company to help keep shared data safe.

toast.warn: Quick heads up, double-check this before it goes out.

aws_access_key.name: AWS access key
aws_access_key.reason: Looks like an AWS access-key ID. Sharing it can grant full account access.

aws_secret_key.name: AWS secret key
aws_secret_key.reason: Looks like an AWS secret key. Treat it like a password and rotate immediately.

anthropic_api_key.name: Anthropic API key
anthropic_api_key.reason: Looks like an Anthropic API key. Sharing it grants billed access to your account.

openai_api_key.name: OpenAI API key
openai_api_key.reason: Looks like an OpenAI API key. Sharing it grants billed access to your account.

github_pat.name: GitHub PAT
github_pat.reason: Looks like a GitHub personal access token. Revoke it if it leaks outside trusted channels.

google_api_key.name: Google API key
google_api_key.reason: Looks like a Google API key. Anyone with this key can call the API on your project.

slack_token.name: Slack token
slack_token.reason: Looks like a Slack token. Sharing it can give bot or user access to your workspace.

stripe_secret.name: Stripe secret
stripe_secret.reason: Looks like a Stripe secret key. Sharing it exposes payment-processing privileges.

private_key_pem.name: Private key (PEM)
private_key_pem.reason: Looks like a private cryptographic key. Never share private keys in chat.

jwt_token.name: JWT
jwt_token.reason: Looks like a JSON Web Token. It may grant authenticated access until it expires.

credit_card.name: Credit card
credit_card.reason: Looks like a credit-card number. Avoid sending payment data through chat.

iban.name: IBAN
iban.reason: Looks like a bank IBAN. Share account numbers only over trusted channels.

generic_api_key.name: API key or password
generic_api_key.reason: Looks like an API key, token, or password written as a key=value pair. Don't paste credentials into chat.

national_id_iran.name: Iran national ID
national_id_iran.reason: Looks like an Iranian national ID. This is highly sensitive personal data.

email.name: Email address
email.reason: Contains an email address. Confirm the recipient is allowed to receive it.

phone_intl.name: Phone number
phone_intl.reason: Contains a phone number. Confirm the recipient is allowed to receive it.

ipv4_private.name: Private IPv4
ipv4_private.reason: Contains a private IPv4 address that may reveal internal network details.

high_entropy_token.name: High-entropy token
high_entropy_token.reason: Looks like a random token or secret. Verify it is not a credential before sending.

internal_hostname.name: Internal hostname
internal_hostname.reason: Matches an internal hostname. Avoid leaking infrastructure details externally.

ai_smart_scan.name: Smart scan
ai_smart_scan.reason: Your message looks like it may contain confidential or restricted information.

events.empty: No events yet. When Content Safety steps in, you will see it here.
events.viewAllHint: Open the Activity tab for the full event log.

errors.incompletePattern: Give every ban a word/phrase (or advanced pattern)
